text:
emma: Quick heads-up — hit a weird telemetry/telemetry-redaction combo in the Python quickstart. When urllib3 Retry triggers an auth-retry (401->refresh->retry) the x-request-id is present in logs before the refresh but missing after. Repro below.

sid: oh no, that will break join keys in our log-based dashboards. Only Python?

emma: only verified in the python sampleapp so far. repro steps: 1) start sampleapp with LOG_FORMAT=json 2) trigger a route that calls downstream with Authorization that gets a 401 then refreshes token and retries 3) check structured logs in stdout — request_id field is null on the retried attempt.

emma: tiny repro (requests + urllib3 Retry):
```py
# repro.py
import requests
from urllib3.util import Retry
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter

s = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=1, status_forcelist=[401], raise_on_status=False)
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
res = s.get('https://svc/internal', headers={'x-request-id':'py-777', 'Authorization':'Bearer bad'})
print(res.status_code)
```

taylor: sounds like our OTEL WSGI middleware or the logging formatter is running before the token-refresh wrapper re-creates the PreparedRequest and copies headers. If the lib rebuilds the PreparedRequest without copying custom headers, the logging instrumentation sees the new request without x-request-id.

emma: interesting wrinkle: in text/plain dev logs we saw "x-request-id":"py-777" on first attempt and then "x-request-id":null on retry; in JSON logs the logging-redaction plugin converted null->"[redacted]" in prod, so dashboards showed masked values rather than a clear loss. That's confusing.

maria: actionable ideas: 1) make the logging redaction plugin treat missing/null separately from masked values (so we can distinguish a dropped header vs masked sensitive value), 2) update Python sampleapp quickstart to show a safe retry pattern or to seed request id into context var that OTEL hook can re-inject, 3) add a lightweight test in sampleapp e2e to simulate auth refresh retries and assert request id preserved.

taylor: for parity, we should check Go/Node too but the attack surface differs per HTTP lib. Longer-term we should add a small middleware helper in all sampleapps that seeds a request-id into context (thread-local/ContextVar/ALS) and the OTEL outgoing hook always injects from that context into outgoing PreparedRequest if missing. Keep an allowlist of safe headers (x-request-id, traceparent, baggage) and explicitly never copy Authorization.

emma: I prototyped a Python ContextVar helper and a tiny change in our otel-wsgi hook to call:
```py
from contextvars import ContextVar
request_id = ContextVar('request_id', default=None)
# middleware sets request_id.set(header or gen)
# otel-outgoing when creating outgoing request: headers.setdefault('x-request-id', request_id.get())
```

maria: perfect. Also open an issue to tweak the redaction plugin behavior so that null/missing vs redacted are distinguishable in JSON logs (we can add a metadata field like "redaction":"masked" vs "redaction":"missing").

telemetry-bot: Created issue #4760: "Python sampleapp: x-request-id lost on urllib3 auth-retry; add ContextVar reinjection + clarify redaction semantics" (assigned devex).

emma: I'll file a PR with the ContextVar middleware + e2e that simulates 401->refresh->retry. tagging @taylor for OTEL hook review. Thanks! :raised_hands:
